etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: The noun is a learned borrowing from Latin maeander, from Maeander (“the river Meander in Asia Minor (now Büyük Menderes in Turkey) known for its winding course”), from Ancient Greek Μαίανδρος (Maíandros); further etymology uncertain, possibly from Proto-Semitic *miʕay- (“intestine”), from *mi- (device preformative) + *waʕay- (“to contain”).
The verb is derived from the noun.
senses: (chiefly in the plural) One of the turns of a crooked or winding course or path.
(figurative) Often in the plural: a tortuous or winding journey or movement; also, a deviation from a route.
